images.text:
Peter: Hello Mother.
Mother: Peter! What a lovely place!
Peter: You can say that again! Would you advise that I drink green tea?
Mother: I would go with a Darjeeling. How is your new job? Did you put forward that proposal? I knew you were very apprehensive.
Peter: I did. But last week I was ready to quit. I felt my overall progress was significantly slow and my skill set wasn't appropriate.

Mother: I know what you mean. Do they not acknowledge your contributions and involvement with the projects?
Peter: Yes. In fact, the boss appreciated my effort.
Mother: How could she not?
Peter: She's a tough boss. She waited until the last minute to send us home.
Mother: I see. That's terrible. I don't understand people like that. How are things there? Is it competitive?

Peter: Almost threatening. There's a lot of tension in the office.
Mother: How uncomfortable!
Peter: Would you suggest confronting her?
Mother: I suggest you don't. If your boss is pleased, you should be fine.
Peter: Miranda's only a co-worker but acts like my superior. Would you recommend quitting my job?
Mother: You're still new, Peter. I would recommend staying away from office politics. Enjoy your time off. Now, let's hurry so we're not late for that jewellery workshop!

Showing Understanding

Remember when having a conversation in English, it is important to show that you are not only listening to someone explaining or telling you something but also showing understanding of their situation and or feelings.
Here is some language you can use to express understanding of someone's situation and/or feelings.

• I'm sorry to hear that.
  • I know what you mean.
  • I knew you were tired/apprehensive/bored.
  • That's terrible/awful/bad.
  • You can say that again!
  • I see. I see what you mean.
  • How uncomfortable/sad/ ridiculous!
  • Thank you!
  • I don't ... (+verb)
We work together but she acts like she's my boss.
I'm sorry to hear that. I don't understand people like that.
Giving and Asking for Advice

In the Business world, at times, you have an idea, a recommendation or plan that you think could work for your company.

It is important to use proper language to offer those ideas for someone to consider.
Here is some language you can use for making and responding to recommendations.

NOTE:
Remember, it is important to use the word ‘suggest' correctly when speaking. The word ‘suggest' is never followed by a direct personal object. We use the preposition “to.”

✗ I don't know much about tea. What would you suggest me?
✓ I don't know much about tea. What would you suggest to me?
